before: The plan was shown in the previous reply: New pricing, Problem / Solution, Nov 16 to Dec 6 (3 weeks, launch in week 3), 4 text posts a week on LinkedIn, 12 drafts to review, Bolta writes it. The user also uses Instagram; the plan left it off, since it needs a picture on every post.

arguments.name: New pricing
arguments.theme: Our new pricing: three plans, one table
arguments.context_notes: Launch day is Dec 1. Three plans. Facts the user gave, nothing else.

steps.why: A launch is problem_solution (guidance; always send a strategy). theme is the writer's goal sentence; cta_text is used word for word. ends_on is a real date: null is ignored, not refused, and the campaign would keep 1 week. Launch day Dec 1 sits in week 3 because weeks start on the start date's weekday (Monday). A campaign made here is text-based, so content_mix is sent with the plan's 4 text posts: left out, the brand's Content defaults or the strategy's mix could carry pictures. Check resolved_content_mix in the reply. Instagram needs a picture, so it stays off a text campaign. Accounts, notes and the page go on the same create call, so the campaign is made with its accounts. Left out, account_ids would come back empty (a mix sent on the create skips the Content defaults' crosspost fill), and with accounts in the workspace and none on the campaign, activating would stall at needs accounts. If the call refuses these fields: the user picks accounts on the campaign's page, then says done.
Only sources that were read reach the writer. Say which failed, and why.

One Bolta check, and it uses credits. Only once resolved_content_mix read back text, blog or email keys (any other: one line to its page, not started here). Never for a campaign the assistant filled with its own drafts.
Read status (active) and schedule_status (not needs_accounts), and next_generation_at: week 1's drafts are written about 2 days before the week, starting around midnight UTC, so say "around".

say: Campaign on for Acme: New pricing, Nov 16 to Dec 6 on LinkedIn. Week 1's drafts land around Sat Nov 14 and wait for your yes. Instagram needs a picture on every post, so it's set up on the campaign page: bolta.ai/dashboard/campaigns/<id>.
never: Starting a campaign and also writing its posts by hand: Bolta would write a second set.
Leaving content_mix out of a campaign made here: the brand's Content defaults or the strategy's mix can carry pictures.
Putting Instagram on a text campaign: its drafts would be held.
